sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises seeing a GP for any bleeding after the menopause, even a small amount of blood, spotting or pink or brown discharge.
The NHS lists bleeding or spotting after the menopause as a main symptom of womb cancer, but it has other, more common causes.
note: NHS womb cancer page and Wales page as summarised

sentence: NHS inform says anyone with vaginal bleeding after the menopause is referred urgently, within two weeks.
A scan of the womb lining is often the first test, and a small sample of the lining may follow.
note: Search summary of PMB pages; may be from trust pages

sentence: Bleeding after the menopause means vaginal bleeding once periods have stopped, and the NHS lists it among the main symptoms of womb cancer.
note: NHS womb cancer page as summarised

sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises seeing a GP even if the amount is small, or if it is spotting or pink or brown discharge.
Bleeding has many possible causes, and cancer is a less common one.
The causes NHS 111 Wales lists include thinning of the vaginal or womb lining from lower oestrogen, benign polyps and a thickened womb lining.
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) can also be linked with bleeding.
note: Search summary of trust pages; Wales page not confirmed

sentence: The NHS advises not waiting to contact a GP, because finding womb cancer early can make it easier to treat.
note: NHS womb cancer page as summarised

sentence: The NHS lists bleeding between periods, unusually heavy periods and a change in vaginal discharge as other possible signs of womb cancer.
note: NHS womb cancer page as summarised

sentence: NHS advice on heavy periods and pelvic pain also lists bleeding between periods or after sex as a reason to see a GP.
note: NHS Wales heavy periods page as summarised

sentence: NHS inform says that a person with vaginal bleeding after the menopause is referred urgently, to be seen within two weeks.
Referral rules can differ between the UK nations, so the exact pathway depends on where the person lives.
The first test is usually a transvaginal ultrasound scan, which measures the thickness of the womb lining.
note: Search summary; wording from trust pages

sentence: A small sample of the womb lining (biopsy) may follow, and some clinics use hysteroscopy, a look inside the womb with a thin camera.
Treatment depends on the cause; for thinning of the vaginal lining it can include local oestrogen cream.
